slides.texte_overlay:
How to be the guest
everyone wants to invite back
Reply to the invitation quickly. A clear yes or no within a day. Hosts plan food and seats, and the guest who answers fast is already their favourite.
Bring something thoughtful. Flowers, a dessert, a good bottle, or something from your trip. Never arrive empty-handed, even to a casual evening.
Offer to help, then follow the host's lead. "Can I do anything?" If they say no, relax and enjoy. If they say yes, do it well and without any fuss.
Talk to people you don't know. Introduce yourself to the other guests, especially the quiet ones. Good guests make the whole party easier for the host.
Bring good conversation. I do five minutes a day of history, art or science, and there's always a fun story ready when the dinner table goes quiet.
slides.texte_sophia: I do five minutes a day on a micro-learning app like the Sophia app. History, art, science. There's always a fun story ready when the table goes quiet.

slides.texte_overlay: Know when to leave. Watch the host's energy. Leaving while things are still lively is better than being the last guest still talking at 2am.
Send a thank-you message the next day. "Thanks for a great evening, the lasagne was incredible." Small, specific thanks guarantee the next invitation.
